problem: Normal and data-only website changes paid the cost of a sitewide public-page visibility crawl and full header-menu readability crawl even when the release-risk classifier had a bounded affected-route set.
root_cause: The browser job always executed two global checks whenever any preview was required; risk_lane was only used for the separate broad high-risk browser contracts.
prevention: Keep sitewide visibility and menu browser checks mandatory for high-risk changes.
For normal-risk changes, use targeted desktop/mobile route verification against the classifier's affected routes.
Map regulatory data changes to a bounded explicit public-route set instead of defaulting to a single generic route.
Do not skip baseline, syntax, static or page-SEO contracts required by the selected lane.
